title: Airport Pickup with Mobility Needs: Confirming the Handoff
description: Plan an airport pickup with mobility needs: confirm airline assistance, vehicle requirements, equipment, companions and the handoff between them.
image_alt: A curved metal handrail beside a pale stone walkway and tall terminal-style windows in soft monochrome light.
body:
Confirm two arrangements before booking an airport pickup with mobility needs: assistance through the terminal and the road vehicle journey. Agree where those arrangements meet, who will be there and how the passenger, companions, bags and mobility equipment will travel. An airline assistance request does not reserve a car, and a car reservation does not confirm every part of the airport handoff.

Start with the traveler's own requirements. A short description of the boarding arrangement and equipment is more useful than a vehicle class name. Get the provider's specific confirmation before relying on the ride.

Arrange terminal assistance with the airline

SFO's accessibility guidance directs passengers to arrange wheelchair assistance through their airline and to identify themselves to airline staff when assistance is needed at the airport. It describes assistance through the terminal to areas such as baggage claim or a vehicle pickup location.

The U.S. Department of Transportation's wheelchair and guided-assistance guidance also explains airline assistance and the importance of telling staff that you are the passenger who requested it. Discuss the arriving flight and handoff with the airline, rather than assuming a note in a reservation tells everyone where you are.

For a departure, confirm how the traveler will connect with airline assistance after the vehicle drop-off. Repeat the check for the return airport; an arrival arrangement is not automatically the departure plan.

Describe how the passenger and equipment will travel

Tell the transportation provider whether the requested arrangement involves a passenger using a vehicle seat with their mobility aid stowed, or remaining seated in a wheelchair during the road journey. These require different confirmations. Do not treat a folding chair's cargo dimensions as confirmation that the passenger's boarding and seating needs can be met.

  • Travelers: count the passenger and every companion, including anyone who needs to remain with them.
  • Equipment: identify each chair, scooter, walker or other mobility aid, its transport dimensions and weight, and any manufacturer handling instructions relevant to the request.
  • Boarding: describe the arrangement the traveler needs, including whether steps can be used and what assistance must be confirmed.
  • Bags: add the complete luggage list so the equipment is considered alongside the required passenger seats.

Ask the provider to confirm the actual vehicle arrangement and the assistance it can provide. A larger vehicle name alone does not establish accessibility, a suitable loading system, safe equipment accommodation or assistance with moving a person. Do not plan on a chauffeur lifting someone or operating unfamiliar equipment unless the required service has been specifically arranged.

If the traveler needs to remain in a wheelchair, seek explicit confirmation of a vehicle and service suitable for that requirement. A standard sedan or SUV booking is not that confirmation. Vans, Sprinters and buses require a quote, and their names do not establish accessibility or availability.

Keep the airline equipment plan separate

Ask the airline where the traveler's own mobility aid will be returned and what device information it needs. DOT's assistive-device guidance covers aircraft stowage, return, damage and delay, including preparation information for the airline. Follow the airline's current process for the specific device and itinerary.

The ground provider needs the equipment as it will actually travel in the vehicle, including any separate parts or cases. Our luggage and equipment measurement guide helps describe that load. Airline acceptance does not establish road-vehicle fit, and vehicle confirmation does not settle flight requirements.

Agree on the exact handoff point

Before travel, confirm the airport, arriving flight, full local date, terminal where known, agreed meeting location and reachable contacts. Ask how the passenger and companions will reach that location with the equipment and luggage, and who will help with each part. If walking or waiting is difficult, discuss that when arranging the handoff.

Do not substitute a generic instruction to wait outside. At SFO, use the current ground transportation information alongside the provider's instructions for the actual booked service. Ask the provider and airline how to connect their arrangements at the agreed location. An airport map does not confirm that a particular vehicle can load or wait at a chosen entrance.

Example: a traveler and companion have arranged airline wheelchair assistance, but the road provider is still checking whether the traveler's folded chair and luggage can be accommodated. The terminal assistance is one confirmed part; the vehicle arrangement remains pending. Keep both statuses visible and obtain the missing confirmation before treating the journey as settled.

Confirm what happens if the handoff changes

Agree who will contact the road provider if deplaning, collecting the mobility aid or reaching the pickup point takes longer than expected. Check the accepted waiting and change terms. Do not assume flight tracking covers every delay after landing or automatically changes the booking.

If equipment is damaged or delayed, speak with airline staff and update the road provider. A replacement aid or revised meeting location may change the required arrangement; obtain acknowledgment rather than relying on the original description. The flight-change checklist can help when the flight or arrival airport changes too.

A pickup confirmation brief you can copy

Airport mobility handoff request
Trip: [airport, local date, arriving flight, destination].
Travelers: [passenger and companions; lead contact].
Road seating and boarding requirement: [describe the requested arrangement].
Mobility equipment: [type/model, transport dimensions, weight, separate parts].
Other luggage: [complete list].
Terminal assistance: [airline arrangement and contact; confirmed or pending].
Proposed handoff: [location and who helps with each part; confirm with both parties].
Please confirm: [actual vehicle arrangement, assistance provided, pickup instructions, complete quote, waiting/change terms and fallback contact].
Return trip: [repeat the requirements and handoff check].

If you are booking for someone else, review this with the traveler and use the passenger handoff checklist. Share practical requirements with the people arranging the journey; keep unnecessary medical history out of a group itinerary.

For a Koast airport transfer inquiry, send the required arrangement to reserve@koastride.com and ask what can be confirmed. This planning guide does not establish that a wheelchair-accessible vehicle or a particular assistance service is available. Choose a provider that can confirm all the requirements for the trip.
